The torch handle includes a pneumatically controlled jaw assembly configured to selectively engage and release an electrode. The jaw assembly includes a first jaw member that is movable relative to a second jaw member, allowing the electrode to be clamped between the two jaw members when required.

A pneumatic cylinder is positioned within the main housing of the torch handle. The pneumatic cylinder is coupled to a shaft, and movement of the shaft actuates the first jaw member relative to the second jaw member. In this manner, the pneumatic cylinder controls the opening and closing action of the jaw assembly.

The main housing also includes a gas passageway that extends through the housing to an exit orifice located within the second jaw member. This passageway allows gas to be delivered through the torch handle and discharged at or near the jaw assembly, including in the vicinity of the engaged electrode.

A flow controller is provided to selectively direct the gas flow. The flow controller can route gas either to the pneumatic cylinder or to the gas passageway. When gas is directed to the gas passageway, the first jaw member moves toward the second jaw member, thereby engaging or gripping the electrode. Conversely, when gas is directed to the pneumatic cylinder, the first jaw member moves away from the second jaw member, releasing the electrode.
outputs.L4:
A torch handle is provided for selectively gripping and releasing an electrode during operation of a torch system. The torch handle includes a main housing configured to receive and support the operating components of the handle. Within the housing is a pneumatically controlled jaw assembly that is movable between an open position and a closed position. In the closed position, the jaw engages and holds the electrode securely in place. In the open position, the jaw releases the electrode so that the electrode may be inserted, removed, or repositioned.

The jaw is operated by a pneumatic control arrangement located within the torch handle. The pneumatic control arrangement may include a pneumatic cylinder coupled to a movable shaft. When pressurized gas is supplied to the pneumatic cylinder, the shaft is displaced in a manner that causes the jaw to move. Depending on the direction of gas flow and the pressure applied, the shaft may drive the jaw toward the electrode to clamp it, or may allow the jaw to move away from the electrode to release it. This arrangement permits the electrode to be engaged and disengaged without requiring manual tightening of the jaw.

Gas is distributed through the torch handle by way of a gas passageway formed in or carried by the main housing. The gas passageway communicates with the pneumatic cylinder and may also communicate with other internal portions of the handle. A flow controller is positioned in the gas flow path to regulate the direction, rate, or amount of gas delivered through the handle. The flow controller may selectively direct gas to the pneumatic cylinder when actuation of the jaw is desired, or may direct gas toward an exit orifice when gas is to be discharged from the handle.

During operation, gas entering the torch handle can therefore serve more than one function. In one operating state, the gas is routed to the pneumatic cylinder to move the shaft and actuate the jaw assembly. This allows the jaw to close around the electrode or open away from the electrode in a controlled manner. In another operating state, the gas is routed through the passageway and out of the exit orifice. This enables the torch handle to manage gas flow internally while maintaining reliable control over the electrode gripping mechanism.

By integrating the pneumatic cylinder, shaft, gas passageway, flow controller, and jaw assembly within the main housing, the torch handle provides a compact and controlled mechanism for electrode retention. The pneumatic jaw allows repeatable opening and closing, while the gas routing arrangement permits gas to be used both for mechanical actuation and for discharge through the torch handle. This design improves control of the electrode engagement process and provides an organized internal gas flow path within the torch handle.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a plasma torch handle with a pneumatic jaw that grips an electrode and includes internal gas routing controlled by a flow controller.
counterfactuals.output: A plasma torch handle includes a body defining an internal gas passage and a pneumatically actuated jaw assembly configured to selectively grip and release an electrode. The jaw assembly is movable between a clamping position, in which the electrode is retained in electrical and mechanical engagement with the torch, and a release position. A flow controller fluidly coupled to the internal gas passage regulates delivery of pressurized gas through the handle and selectively directs gas to the jaw assembly to actuate gripping of the electrode and to one or more torch gas outlets for plasma generation, cooling, shielding, or purging. The integrated pneumatic gripping and gas-routing arrangement enables controlled electrode retention and gas distribution within the handle while reducing external connections and facilitating electrode replacement.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise invention summary describing a torch handle where gas is selectively directed either to a pneumatic cylinder for jaw actuation or to a passageway ending in an orifice in the jaw.
counterfactuals.output: A torch handle includes an internal gas flow control arrangement configured to selectively route pressurized gas to different functional outputs. In a first operating state, the gas is directed to a pneumatic cylinder to actuate a movable jaw between open and closed positions. In a second operating state, the gas is directed through a passageway extending toward the jaw and terminating at an orifice formed in or adjacent the jaw. The orifice discharges the gas at the jaw region, for example to provide a purge, cooling, cleaning, or process gas flow. A selector valve or control member in the handle switches the gas supply between the pneumatic cylinder and the jaw orifice passageway, allowing a common gas source to be used for both jaw actuation and localized gas delivery.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate patent application language for a system inside a torch handle that uses a pneumatic cylinder, shaft, movable jaw member, fixed jaw member, and gas passageway to engage an electrode.
counterfactuals.output:
Below is example patent-application-style language directed to a torch handle having an internal pneumatic clamping system for engaging an electrode.

---

## Title

**Torch Handle Having Pneumatically Actuated Electrode Engagement Mechanism**

---

## Abstract

A torch handle includes a body having a gas passageway and an electrode receiving region. A fixed jaw member is disposed within the torch handle and a movable jaw member is movable relative to the fixed jaw member to selectively engage an electrode. A pneumatic cylinder disposed within the torch handle is operatively coupled to the movable jaw member by a shaft. Application of pressurized gas to the pneumatic cylinder displaces the shaft and moves the movable jaw member between an open position and a clamping position. In the clamping position, the movable jaw member urges the electrode against the fixed jaw member to mechanically and electrically engage the electrode. The gas passageway may be configured to supply process gas through the torch handle and/or actuating gas to the pneumatic cylinder.

---

## Technical Field

The present disclosure relates generally to welding, cutting, gouging, or plasma torch assemblies and, more particularly, to a torch handle having an internal pneumatically actuated mechanism for selectively engaging and retaining an electrode.

---

## Background

Torch assemblies commonly employ electrodes that must be secured within a torch body or handle to provide electrical continuity, mechanical retention, and proper alignment with a gas flow path. Conventional electrode retention mechanisms may require threaded engagement, manual tightening, springs, collets, or externally accessible locking components. Such arrangements can increase electrode replacement time, require operator dexterity, or result in inconsistent clamping force.

Accordingly, there is a need for a torch handle having an integrated actuation system capable of selectively engaging an electrode in a controlled and repeatable manner.

---

## Summary

In one aspect, a torch handle includes a housing, a fixed jaw member, a movable jaw member, a pneumatic cylinder, a shaft, and a gas passageway. The fixed jaw member is positioned to engage a first portion of an electrode. The movable jaw member is disposed opposite the fixed jaw member and is movable between an open position and a clamping position. The pneumatic cylinder is positioned within the torch handle and includes a piston movable in response to pressurized gas. The shaft is coupled between the piston and the movable jaw member such that movement of the piston causes movement of the movable jaw member. The gas passageway extends through at least a portion of the torch handle and is configured to deliver gas to the pneumatic cylinder and/or toward a torch operating region.

In another aspect, pressurized gas supplied through the gas passageway actuates the pneumatic cylinder to move the shaft and the movable jaw member toward the fixed jaw member, thereby clamping an electrode between the movable jaw member and the fixed jaw member.

In another aspect, release or reduction of gas pressure permits the movable jaw member to move away from the fixed jaw member to allow insertion or removal of the electrode.

---

## Detailed Description

A torch handle includes an elongate handle body defining an interior cavity. The handle body may be formed from an electrically insulating material, a thermally resistant material, or a combination of conductive and nonconductive components. The handle body includes an electrode receiving opening configured to receive at least a portion of an electrode into the torch handle.

A fixed jaw member is disposed in the handle body adjacent the electrode receiving opening. The fixed jaw member may include a contact surface shaped to engage a corresponding surface of the electrode. In some embodiments, the fixed jaw member is electrically conductive and forms part of an electrical current path between a power supply and the electrode. The fixed jaw member may be mounted in a stationary position relative to the handle body.

A movable jaw member is disposed opposite the fixed jaw member. The movable jaw member includes a contact surface facing the fixed jaw member. The movable jaw member is movable between an open position, in which the electrode can be inserted between or removed from the fixed and movable jaw members, and a clamping position, in which the electrode is compressed or captured between the movable jaw member and the fixed jaw member. The contact surfaces of the fixed and movable jaw members may be planar, arcuate, V-shaped, serrated, textured, or otherwise configured to improve retention and/or electrical contact with the electrode.

A pneumatic cylinder is positioned within the torch handle. The pneumatic cylinder includes a cylinder bore and a piston movable within the bore. A shaft is operatively connected to the piston and extends from the pneumatic cylinder toward the movable jaw member. The shaft may be directly coupled to the movable jaw member or may be coupled through a linkage, lever, cam, wedge, or pivoting member. Movement of the piston within the pneumatic cylinder causes corresponding movement of the shaft, which in turn moves the movable jaw member relative to the fixed jaw member.

A gas passageway extends through at least a portion of the torch handle. The gas passageway may be connected to a source of pressurized gas. In some embodiments, the gas passageway supplies actuating gas to the pneumatic cylinder. In some embodiments, the gas passageway also supplies process gas to a distal region of the torch. The gas passageway may include one or more branches, valves, restrictions, seals, ports, or fittings for directing gas to the pneumatic cylinder and/or to a torch gas outlet.

During operation, an electrode is inserted into the electrode receiving opening and positioned between the fixed jaw member and the movable jaw member. Pressurized gas is supplied to the pneumatic cylinder through the gas passageway. The pressurized gas acts on the piston, causing the piston and shaft to move. Movement of the shaft drives the movable jaw member toward the fixed jaw member, thereby engaging the electrode. The engagement may retain the electrode mechanically, align the electrode, and establish electrical contact between the electrode and one or more conductive components of the torch.

To release the electrode, gas pressure in the pneumatic cylinder may be vented, reduced, or redirected. The movable jaw member may then move away from the fixed jaw member under the influence of a return spring, resilient member, reverse pneumatic pressure, gravity, manual force, or stored elastic energy in the mechanism. Once the movable jaw member is in the open position, the electrode may be removed or replaced.

In some embodiments, the pneumatic cylinder is a single-acting cylinder biased toward the open position by a spring. In other embodiments, the pneumatic cylinder is biased toward the clamping position and gas pressure is used to release the electrode. In further embodiments, the pneumatic cylinder is a double-acting cylinder having first and second gas chambers for selectively moving the movable jaw member in opposite directions.

The shaft may extend generally parallel to a longitudinal axis of the torch handle, generally transverse to the longitudinal axis, or at an oblique angle. The movable jaw member may translate linearly, pivot about a pivot point, or move along a curved or guided path. The movable jaw member may include a wedge surface engaged by the shaft such that axial movement of the shaft produces lateral clamping movement of the movable jaw member.

Seals may be provided around the pneumatic cylinder, shaft, and gas passageway to inhibit gas leakage. Electrical insulation may be provided between the pneumatic cylinder and conductive torch components where desired. Alternatively, one or more portions of the pneumatic cylinder, shaft, fixed jaw member, or movable jaw member may be electrically conductive and may form part of an electrical path to the electrode.

---

## Example Independent Claim

1. **A torch handle assembly**, comprising:  
   a handle body defining an interior cavity and an electrode receiving region;  
   a fixed jaw member disposed at least partially within the handle body and positioned to engage an electrode received in the electrode receiving region;  
   a movable jaw member disposed at least partially within the handle body and movable relative to the fixed jaw member between an open position and a clamping position;  
   a pneumatic cylinder disposed within the handle body;  
   a shaft operatively coupling the pneumatic cylinder to the movable jaw member; and  
   a gas passageway extending through at least a portion of the handle body and in fluid communication with the pneumatic cylinder;  
   wherein pressurized gas supplied through the gas passageway actuates the pneumatic cylinder to move the shaft and thereby move the movable jaw member toward the fixed jaw member to engage the electrode between the movable jaw member and the fixed jaw member.

---

## Example Dependent Claims

2. The torch handle assembly of claim 1, wherein the fixed jaw member is electrically conductive and is configured to provide electrical continuity to the electrode.

3. The torch handle assembly of claim 1, wherein the movable jaw member is electrically conductive and is configured to provide electrical continuity to the electrode.

4. The torch handle assembly of claim 1, wherein the pneumatic cylinder comprises a piston movable within a cylinder bore, and wherein the shaft is coupled to the piston.

5. The torch handle assembly of claim 1, further comprising a return spring configured to bias the movable jaw member toward the open position.

6. The torch handle assembly of claim 1, wherein the pneumatic cylinder is a single-acting pneumatic cylinder.

7. The torch handle assembly of claim 1, wherein the pneumatic cylinder is a double-acting pneumatic cylinder.

8. The torch handle assembly of claim 1, wherein the gas passageway is further configured to deliver process gas toward a distal end of the torch handle.

9. The torch handle assembly of claim 1, wherein the gas passageway includes a first branch in fluid communication with the pneumatic cylinder and a second branch configured to deliver process gas to a torch operating region.

10. The torch handle assembly of claim 1, wherein the movable jaw member is configured to translate linearly relative to the fixed jaw member.

11. The torch handle assembly of claim 1, wherein the movable jaw member is configured to pivot relative to the fixed jaw member.

12. The torch handle assembly of claim 1, wherein the shaft engages a wedge surface associated with the movable jaw member to convert axial movement of the shaft into clamping movement of the movable jaw member.

13. The torch handle assembly of claim 1, wherein at least one of the fixed jaw member or the movable jaw member includes a textured electrode-contacting surface.

14. The torch handle assembly of claim 1, further comprising a seal disposed between the pneumatic cylinder and the gas passageway.

15. The torch handle assembly of claim 1, wherein venting of gas from the pneumatic cylinder permits the movable jaw member to move away from the fixed jaw member to release the electrode.

16. The torch handle assembly of claim 1, wherein the pneumatic cylinder, the shaft, the movable jaw member, and the fixed jaw member are all disposed within the handle body.

17. The torch handle assembly of claim 1, wherein the electrode receiving region is aligned with a longitudinal axis of the handle body.

18. The torch handle assembly of claim 1, wherein the shaft extends generally parallel to a longitudinal axis of the handle body.

19. The torch handle assembly of claim 1, wherein the shaft extends generally transverse to a longitudinal axis of the handle body.

20. The torch handle assembly of claim 1, wherein the movable jaw member is configured to apply a clamping force to the electrode in response to gas pressure within the pneumatic cylinder.

---

## Example Method Claim

21. **A method of engaging an electrode in a torch handle**, comprising:  
   inserting an electrode into an electrode receiving region of a torch handle;  
   supplying pressurized gas through a gas passageway in the torch handle to a pneumatic cylinder disposed within the torch handle;  
   moving a shaft coupled to the pneumatic cylinder in response to the pressurized gas;  
   moving a movable jaw member relative to a fixed jaw member using the shaft; and  
   clamping the electrode between the movable jaw member and the fixed jaw member.

22. The method of claim 21, further comprising venting gas from the pneumatic cylinder to move the movable jaw member away from the fixed jaw member and release the electrode.

23. The method of claim 21, further comprising delivering process gas through the torch handle using the gas passageway.

---

## Alternative Broad Claim Form

1. **An electrode retention system for a torch handle**, comprising:  
   a fixed electrode-contacting member;  
   a movable electrode-contacting member movable relative to the fixed electrode-contacting member;  
   a pneumatic actuator positioned within the torch handle;  
   a force-transmitting shaft extending between the pneumatic actuator and the movable electrode-contacting member; and  
   a gas flow path configured to provide pressurized gas to the pneumatic actuator;  
   wherein actuation of the pneumatic actuator displaces the force-transmitting shaft to urge the movable electrode-contacting member toward the fixed electrode-contacting member and thereby retain an electrode.
